observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect energy conversion technique as No2, did not exploit and convert the A/C energy in order to maintain the tactical formation position during the turns, with the result that lateral separation opened to 1500 feet and line abreast deviation reached 45 degrees. The IP had to direct the geometry and execute part of the correction to restore the briefed position. Further practice in position keeping as No2 is required.

SP, due to an unagreed division of lookout responsibility within the formation, did not maintain the visual reference on the Leader and did not execute the visual signals given during the maneuver, with the result that the recovery heading was missed by 45 degrees and altitude went 800 feet low. The correction could not be completed without assistance and the IP directed the reposition and flew part of the recovery. Formation lookout and visual signal responsibilities as No2 require further study.

SP, due to a late application of the corrections required to alleviate deviations from the tactical formation position, allowed line abreast deviation to reach 30 degrees and lateral separation 1000 feet during the tactical turns. The position as No2 was restored only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the deviations were recognized and corrected with delay. Familiarity with the correction technique described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is expected to improve.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the fuel state during the working phase of the sortie, did not use the engine with consideration to the fuel reserve while regaining position as No2, with the result that entry/exit speed reached 30 knots above the briefed value and altitude 1000 feet high. Both the energy management and the fuel check were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP maintained position as No2 within the desired standards, executing clearing at the proper area and responding to the visual signals given by the Leader. However, line abreast deviation twice reached 18 degrees and lateral separation 700 feet before the corrections were applied, and altitude was allowed to build 700 feet high in one tactical turn. The deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in the timely application of position corrections is expected to improve.

SP executed clearing at the proper area as No2 and applied the proper corrections promptly, holding line abreast deviation within 8 degrees, lateral separation within 400 feet and altitude within 250 feet throughout the tactical turns. Energy was exploited and converted correctly, with entry/exit speed within 10 knots and sustained Gs within 0.3 of the briefed value. All visual signals given by the Leader were recognized and executed without delay, and engine handling showed consideration of the fuel reserve. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP maintained the tactical formation position as No2 with negligible deviations during all the phases of flight, line abreast deviation not exceeding 3 degrees, lateral separation held within 100 feet, altitude within 100 feet and recovery heading within 3 degrees. Clearing was executed at the proper area throughout, all visual signals given by the Leader were answered immediately, and the A/C energy was converted with precise anticipation of the Leader's turns. Engine use showed constant consideration of the fuel reserve. Accuracy was exceptional and above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
